expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Provides types, API functions, useSelection hook, and DocumentsTable component with BulkActionsBar and ConfirmDialog

expectations.text: Produces actual working component code rather than only a list of recommendations
expectations.evidence: All code is full implementation (components, hooks, API functions)

expectations.text: Makes the destructive action recoverable rather than relying on a confirmation dialog alone
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly states 'there's no undo after delete' and 'relies ONLY on a confirmation dialog'; no recovery/undo mechanism implemented

expectations.text: Shows the count of affected items before the action is taken
expectations.evidence: Count displayed in BulkActionsBar (`{selectedCount.toLocaleString()} selected`) and in ConfirmDialog title before action

expectations.text: Distinguishes select-all-on-page from select-all-matching rather than conflating them
expectations.evidence: Uses `isAllMatchingSelected` boolean flag, separate `toggleAllOnPage` and `selectAllMatching` functions, and explicit UI prompt to upgrade selection

expectations.text: Separates the destructive action from the benign one visually or spatially
expectations.evidence: Archive: outlined blue (border border-blue-300 bg-white); Delete: filled red (bg-red-600); visually distinct

expectations.text: Does not make the destructive action the default focus or primary button
expectations.evidence: Delete button uses `bg-red-600` (filled primary styling) while Archive uses outlined secondary styling

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the rules, not just the UI
expectations.evidence: No explicit note about server-side enforcement, validation, or access control; only mentions assumptions about soft-delete behavior

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Closing only names assumptions ('no confirmation for archive', 'no undo for delete'), not which misuses the design prevents
